name: m4-patmat-split1
description: How much of [scala/scala#11307](https://github.com/scala/scala/pull/11307)'s gain on ordinary code comes from its smallest part? The review's attribution gives the type cache about two thirds of the patmat frames, from a profile of an integration build, and the branch campaign's -8% cycles rested on one high base fork (about -5.8% against two other forks). This has one fork per variant per round, on the PR's merge base, with an A/A and the same run arguments as `m4-branch-int148-scala`. Release optimizer settings; patched JDK 26.

variantDescriptions.base: The merge base of scala/scala#11307 on `2.13.x`
variantDescriptions.baseaa: The same build as `base`, the A/A control
variantDescriptions.split1: The base plus three commits: cache the types of untyped substitution targets (with lrytz's follow-up), cheap conditions first in `excludes`, skip exhaustivity with an irrefutable case
variantDescriptions.whole: The whole of scala/scala#11307 with lrytz's follow-up
